title: Continuous integration and per-pull-request preview environments

videos.script:
Lesson 1 ended with a host that builds every push. This lesson puts something in front of that build. A machine that checks every pull request before anybody merges it.

{{lockfile}} It starts with how that machine installs. Not npm install, but npm ci, which trusts the lockfile and nothing else. You will see it refuse a lockfile that disagrees with package.json.

{{test}} Then the planner gets its first tests, with Vitest, for the functions that total a week. And you will watch a clean copy of the repository fail on a file you forgot to commit, which is the one bug your own computer can never show you.

{{workflow}} Then the GitHub Actions workflow that runs all of it, line by line, and the rule that makes its result matter: no merge while it is red.

{{previews}} And previews. Every pull request built at an address of its own, so a reviewer clicks instead of imagining. You will build two branches side by side on your computer, the way a host does. And see why a preview is public, and what must never be in one.
